name: How should I arrange the sink, refrigerator, and stove in an open-concept kitchen?

mainEntity.name: How should I arrange the sink, refrigerator, and stove in an open-concept kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text:
## Direct answer
The refrigerator, sink, and cooktop should form an efficient work pattern without forcing people to cross the main walking route. In an open plan, the layout must also keep cleanup, cooking, and entertaining from competing for the same space.

## Context
A beautiful kitchen can feel frustrating when the refrigerator opens into a walkway, the dishwasher blocks the sink, or guests stand beside the cooktop. Sightlines should support conversation while keeping hot surfaces and active work zones protected.

## Key factors
- Frequency and style of cooking.
- Refrigerator access for family and guests.
- Dishwasher location relative to cabinets and sink.
- Separation between work aisles and through-traffic.

## Practical guidance
Draw the kitchen around actual movements: unload groceries, wash produce, prepare food, cook, serve, eat, and clean up. Use appliance-door templates and test the routes before ordering cabinetry.

## Soft positioning
Elite Remodeling & Design develops layouts around intended use, existing conditions, storage, and everyday function.
acceptedAnswer.description: Arrange them so food preparation has a logical sequence while the main walking route stays clear. Test grocery unloading, produce washing, cooking, serving, and cleanup with appliance-door templates before finalizing cabinet locations.
